clocks.label: KYIV PAUSE ENDS
clocks.why: The 72-hour instruction that no strikes hit either capital, which covered the Witkoff and Kushner shuttle, runs out tomorrow. This is the dated falsifier on GEO-005, held at 20 today for a second session: if it lapses with no extension and no jointly acknowledged text - no demarcation line, no named monitor, no guarantor - the number goes to 17 and the 3 September raise is scored a miss rather than deferred.

clocks.label: FOMC DECISION
clocks.why: The meeting behind GEO-029 at 63 per cent. July held at 3.50-3.75 with THREE members dissenting FOR a hike; PCE runs 3.7 per cent year-on-year. This is the clock that decides whether the world's reserve central bank tightens INTO an oil supply shock - the 1973-74 error in either direction - with the ten-year already through our 4.75 red line and Brent 2.5 per cent under $100.

clocks.label: BOJ DECISION
clocks.why: Two days after the Fed, and the clock behind GEO-025, RAISED to 29 today. The yen is at 154.06 on hike bets, past the July joint-intervention peak, with 3.7 of the required 8 per cent already done. The carry unwind needs both legs - a Tokyo surprise and a dovish repricing of the Fed - and the Fed leg is the one currently missing, which is exactly why this is 29 and not 40.

clocks.label: BERLIN + MV VOTE
clocks.why: Two more Land elections thirteen days after Saxony-Anhalt, and the first test of whether 43.9 per cent was a Land-specific result or a national repricing. This prices GEO-028 at 23 and the new SAXONY-ANHALT THIRD BALLOT wire: a second AfD plurality in a different kind of Land - Berlin is urban and western in character, Mecklenburg-Vorpommern eastern and rural - would make the arithmetic argument general rather than local.

clocks.label: HORMUZ FALSIFIER
clocks.why: Our own dated falsifier, published in advance so it can be scored against us, and now carrying a second leg. Leg one: an attack on a laden tanker inside the INTERNATIONAL LANES. Leg two, added today: Iran publishing coordinates for its new restricted zone, or Oman co-signing a corridor map. If neither occurs by this date, the escalation read is a MISS - GEO-001 back toward 21, GEO-003 back to about 38, and the zone is scored as rhetoric.

clocks.label: XI SUMMIT
clocks.why: The state visit GEO-006 rides at 89 per cent and GEO-012 at 31, and the date Washington wants its 7.5 per cent overcapacity finding published before. Brent's band question resolves the SAME DAY on a daily CLOSE - this board's first Brier score in 29 open forecasts, and the reason today's $97.93 intraday print did not count.

speculation.obs: The strait's traffic count and the strait's visible traffic count are no longer the same number. Windward's daily maritime-intelligence tracking recorded four vessels - two tankers, a bulk carrier and a liquid-service vessel - transiting the Strait of Hormuz on 6 September with AIS switched off, one inbound and three outbound. Kpler's separate count put total commodity transits that day at six. Read together, two independent commercial trackers say most of Sunday's movement through the world's most important chokepoint was dark.
speculation.src: Windward Daily Intelligence (Strait of Hormuz tracker), cross-read against Kpler transit counts reported by Reuters
speculation.read: Labelled inference, and the load-bearing observation is the ratio, not either count on its own. If four of roughly six transits ran without transponders, then the published transit statistics everyone is quoting are a measurement of the compliant minority, and the real question stops being how much is moving and becomes who is willing to be seen moving. That fits the permit reading: a ship going dark is not hiding from the sea, it is hiding from one of the two lists. The honest alternative is duller and should be said - AIS goes off routinely near conflict zones for crew safety, and a four-vessel sample on one day is a thin base to build a regime on.
speculation.falsifier: A run of days where dark transits are a small minority of the total, published by the same tracker, kills the reading that darkness has become the norm. A trade-press or insurer report describing owners instructing masters to run dark specifically to avoid appearing on an American or Iranian list would confirm it and move this to corroborated.

speculation.obs: The ship Kim Jong Un commissioned on Sunday is one that imagery analysts had already logged as barely able to move. As published by Daily NK's satellite-analysis desk, the 5,000-tonne Kang Kon - which capsized at its own launch at Chongjin in May 2025 and was righted under visible political pressure - has since been observed sitting at a fixed berth with little independent sea time, with signs the vessel has difficulty navigating on its own. The same analysis puts a third destroyer at Nampo at roughly 30 per cent complete, and reads activity at Chongjin as possible preparation for hulls larger than 5,000 tonnes.
speculation.src: Daily NK satellite-analysis desk, with related port-upgrade imagery reporting by Radio Free Asia in June 2026
speculation.read: Labelled inference, and the load-bearing observation is berth time rather than steel. A warship that does not go to sea is not a deterrent, it is a monument - and the ceremony declaring the Kang Kon part of the state nuclear response system was held for a hull the trackers say has hardly moved. The reading that fits both facts is that the announcement is the deliverable: North Korea is buying planning burden in Seoul and Tokyo at ceremony prices, which is a rational trade for a state that cannot afford a real blue-water navy. Note the alternative that would be embarrassing to miss - a ship kept at a berth may be working up rather than broken, and commissioning is sometimes the start of sea trials rather than a substitute for them.
speculation.falsifier: Repeated multi-day patrols east of the peninsula, or a photographed missile launch from the Kang Kon at sea, kills the monument read outright and upgrades this to a real capability. Continued berth-bound imagery through the autumn, or a second independent imagery desk - CSIS Beyond Parallel, Planet, Maxar - describing the same immobility, moves it to corroborated.

speculation.obs: A satellite-analysis team has watched two months of construction go up at China's most secretive flight-test base, and the hangars are the wrong size for fighters. As published by Misbar's team at Al-Araby TV, a comparison of European Sentinel-2 imagery from 2 July and 1 September 2026 shows a marked acceleration at Lop Nur air base in Xinjiang: a new concrete taxiway running parallel to the roughly five-kilometre main runway now nearly complete, a newly connected 130-metre circular apron at the northern end, and four large structures under construction on the western side, each around 80 metres wide.
speculation.src: Misbar / Al-Araby TV analysis team, published 3 September 2026, using European Space Agency Sentinel-2 imagery dated 2 July and 1 September 2026
speculation.read: Labelled inference. The load-bearing observation is the hangar width, not the runway - 80 metres is built for large wingspans, not for fighters, and the analysts read it as capacity for something in the strategic-bomber or large-airframe class. Lop Nur is already the venue where imagery caught what are described as sixth-generation prototypes, the J-36 and J-XDS, in the previous year. The reason this belongs on a geopolitical board rather than an aviation one is timing: infrastructure is the slowest and most honest signal a state emits, because you cannot fake a taxiway, and this one is being poured on a schedule that fits a stated 2030 deployment ambition. Sentinel-2 is free and public, so the claim is checkable by anyone with the coordinates - which is why the grade is credible rather than corroborated, pending a second imagery house.
speculation.falsifier: A second independent imagery analysis - Planet, Maxar, or a defence-research institute - describing the same structures at the same dimensions upgrades this to corroborated. Hangars completing at a width consistent with fighters, or the structures turning out to be maintenance or storage sheds, kills the large-airframe read outright.

dossiers.name: Iran

glance.government: Islamic Republic - a clerical-military hybrid in which the security institutions have been ascendant since the February-May war
glance.leader: Mojtaba Khamenei, Supreme Leader since 8 Mar 2026, not verifiably seen in public for roughly six months; Masoud Pezeshkian president; IRGC commander-in-chief Ahmad Vahidi the operative center
glance.gdp: Roughly $300-390bn nominal depending on source; forecast to contract about 5% in 2026 with inflation near 70% and the rial at a record 2.02m to the dollar
glance.military: About 570,000-610,000 active (IISS puts it near 570,000) plus roughly 350,000 reserves; the IRGC Navy, not the regular navy, holds the strait
glance.influence: Transit rights and mine inventory at Hormuz, anti-ship missiles, Iraqi and Yemeni networks - set against oil revenue the central bank governor himself describes as having fallen to zero

dossiers.summary: Start with the constraint, not the man. Iran is a state whose one convertible asset - the barrel - has stopped moving, which is why its remaining leverage is geographic rather than economic, and why it is spent in advertised doses rather than banked. The desk that decides is the IRGC Navy and the new wartime security committee, not the presidency and not the invisible Leader: Washington routed its own peace offer through career Guard commanders, and Iran's president has said on state television that communicating with Khamenei is very difficult. That produces exactly the behaviour this board keeps recording - a volley at forewarned bases in Jordan that was almost entirely intercepted, mines laid and lanes conditionally cleared, six near-breakthroughs that each end in a restated condition. Prospect theory says a cornered regime gambles, but a regime whose survival runs through an institution that profits from the crisis has an interest in holding the temperature where it can still choose it. The falsifier is a strike that actually kills Americans, or a verified minesweeping calendar with published coordinates - either would show the temperature is no longer being chosen.

concerns: Mine and anti-ship capability at Hormuz is intact and reversible - a cleared lane is a maintenance schedule, not a settlement
Succession is unresolved in practice: an unseen Leader plus an IRGC that answers Washington's messages is a leadership fiction with a real chain of command underneath
Oil revenue near zero against 70% inflation removes the economic off-ramp that would normally price restraint
Escalation is now probabilistic rather than intentional - interception rates, not decisions, separate a message from a casualty event

Retaliation has gone HORIZONTAL: fire into US facilities in Jordan, Bahrain and Kuwait in a single night widens the number of surfaces on which the interception equilibrium can fail, and converts Gulf hosts from venues into potential parties

The war has reached the LOADING POINT: Iranian state media says four US missiles hit a tanker six miles off Kharg on 5 September, and Iran fired anti-ship and ballistic missiles toward the strait the day before. Unconfirmed, and the terminals themselves are still unstruck - but the one asset with any convertible value left is now inside the target set

dossiers.name: Russia

glance.government: Presidential autocracy with a managed legislature; State Duma elections due September 2026
glance.leader: Vladimir Putin - the only decider on the war file; Peskov is a thermostat, not an actor
glance.population: About 144 million (2026 estimate; occupied-territory counting disputed)
glance.gdp: Roughly $2.7tn nominal; the government cut its 2026 growth forecast toward 0.4-1%, with oil and gas revenue reported down more than 25%
glance.military: About 1.3 million active with roughly 2 million reserves; defence spending near 6.3-6.5% of GDP
glance.influence: Sanctioned-barrel logistics including the Arctic route, Africa Corps guarantees in the Sahel, energy leverage over Europe, veto and nuclear status

dossiers.summary: Moscow's constraint is refining and money, not morale. Ukrainian deep strikes have pushed refinery runs to about 3.6m barrels a day, the lowest since 2002, and the fuel export ban first imposed in July is being weighed for a second extension - each extension a public admission of how much capacity is offline. The deciding desks are the defence and finance ministries rather than the foreign ministry: the September Duma election and the 6.3-6.5% of GDP the war costs are what price the negotiating posture, which is why the deep pause Peskov announced reads as a bargaining position taken from a front that is still moving at Pokrovsk. Watch where the state chose to spend a scarce asset this weekend - Africa Corps, roughly 200-300 personnel supplied overland through Burkina Faso, was used to save a junta in Niamey, buying an advertisement and incurring an obligation in the same act. The observables that would move this file are not statements but airlift and diesel: Flight Unit 224 traffic above its six-flight run rate, or refinery runs recovering past 4m barrels a day.

concerns: The fuel and refining constraint is the real bind - denial is working where punishment has not, and Kyiv is aiming at exactly that
The announced campaign against Ukraine's grid is punishment by Pape's definition, with a poor historical conversion into concessions
Sahel guarantees now carry a defend-the-palace obligation a 200-300 person detachment cannot scale
September Duma elections and a possible post-election reserve call-up are the domestic clock every diplomatic signal is priced against

The covert front against the supplier coalition is now formally attributed: Berlin blames Moscow for an explosive drone at Leipzig/Halle and closes the Bonn consulate on Sept 18, with the EU calling it state-sponsored terrorism - salami tactics against logistics rather than against forces

First reciprocated pause of the war, and it is a bargaining instrument rather than fatigue: Putin ordered no strikes on Kyiv for 72 hours from midnight on 5 September, explicitly tied to the American envoys' visit, hours after striking Ukrainian airports and infrastructure and with Ryabkov restating that Washington must accept realities on the ground

dossiers.name: Ukraine

glance.government: Wartime presidential republic under martial law; national elections suspended for the duration
glance.leader: Volodymyr Zelenskyy, constrained by coalition dependence; Rustem Umerov holds both the negotiating brief and the intelligence file
glance.population: About 39.5 million on mid-2026 estimates - wartime displacement makes every figure soft
glance.gdp: Roughly $225bn nominal (2025); the EU agreed a package of about EUR 90bn for 2026-27, funded by market borrowing rather than by seizing the roughly EUR 210bn of frozen Russian assets
glance.military: About 677,000 active on the IISS count; larger figures circulate and are not verified
glance.influence: A deep-strike drone campaign that has taken Russian refining to a 24-year low, the Black Sea corridor, and the political weight of being the coalition's test case

dossiers.summary: Kyiv's constraint is arithmetic - manpower, interceptors and a donor calendar - and it sets the strategy rather than following from it. The one instrument Ukraine owns outright is the drone campaign against Russian refineries, which is denial in Pape's sense and is measurably working; nearly everything else is rented from capitals that vote. That dependence is why the deciding desk is now split between the general staff and a negotiating channel run through Washington, and why Zelenskyy has to say yes to the joint Western plan and no to surrender in the same breath. It also explains Myla: an army under sustained deep strike disperses munitions into settlements, which lowers the odds of losing a depot and raises the odds of a night like Friday's, when 38 people died mostly from what the warehouse contained. The falsifiable claim for the winter is that Russia's fuel constraint shapes Russian behaviour more than blackouts shape Ukrainian negotiating positions - if Kyiv's position visibly softens under grid attack while Moscow's does not under fuel shortage, the model is wrong and we say so.

concerns: The announced Russian campaign against the electricity grid arrives with winter and with air-defence stocks already rationed
Pokrovsk is the axis Moscow names when it explains why it is in no hurry to talk; its fall would be a step change, not a line move
Funding is market-borrowed rather than asset-backed, which puts the money on a European political calendar
Dispersal of munitions into inhabited areas makes mass-casualty events recurrent regardless of anyone's aimpoint

dossiers.name: China

glance.government: Party-state under the most centralized leadership since Mao; a recent command purge reshaped the military timetable
glance.leader: Xi Jinping; Wang Yi carries the foreign file with delegated authority
glance.gdp: About $20.9tn nominal (IMF, 2026); 4.7% growth in the first half against a 4.5-5% target, July exports up 23.9% year on year
glance.military: About 2.0 million active, the largest standing force in the world; announced defence budget in the $280bn range
glance.influence: Buyer of last resort for sanctioned barrels, rare earths and the export machine, coast-guard jurisdiction pressure around Taiwan and the East China Sea, and a summit Washington wants

dossiers.summary: Beijing's constraint this quarter is the calendar, not the doctrine. A state visit on 24 September and a tariff truce expiring in November are both worth more than any concession on Iranian crude, which is why the buying continues while the rhetoric stays defiant - and why Treasury sanctioned an Egyptian bank's UAE branches rather than a Chinese one. An enforcer that keeps picking the cheapest nail is telling you which nail is expensive. The desk to watch is not the foreign ministry but the coast guard and the customs administration: PLA sorties around Taiwan have been declining while jurisdictional assertion has been rising, and that ratchet - salami tactics in Schelling's sense, slices too thin to fight over individually - is the actual instrument. Read the summit as accumulation under cover of detente rather than as a thaw, and keep the discount small: announced head-of-state visits with active staff preparation happen about 90% of the time. The tell that breaks the benign read is a coast-guard action inside the visit window; the tell that breaks the leverage read is a blocking designation on a top-ten Chinese bank before 24 September.

concerns: Coast-guard normalization and seabed mapping are precondition-building around Taiwan, not the event itself
China is the load-bearing leak in the Iran sanctions siege - Mulder's rule is that a siege is only as tight as its leakage path
The tariff truce expires in November, just after the summit, which is where a cheap concession becomes an expensive one
A defiant public line paired with quiet compliance makes intent unreadable from statements; only flows settle it

dossiers.name: Israel

glance.government: Parliamentary democracy; the Knesset dissolved in July and the election is set for 27 October 2026
glance.leader: Benjamin Netanyahu, prime minister; Israel Katz defence minister and the cabinet's designated hawk
glance.gdp: About $720bn nominal on 2026 estimates, with defence spending near 8% of GDP
glance.influence: Air superiority over the Levant, the Washington relationship, and an undeclared nuclear status the state has never confirmed

dossiers.summary: Read every Israeli decision for the next seven weeks through 27 October. That is the constraint, and it is a calendar rather than a character: a prime minister facing an election needs deliverables that are visible, mapped and finished, which is exactly what a declared security zone is. On 4 September Katz said the capture of the Ali al-Taher ridge completes the phase of securing control in southern Lebanon and that there will be no withdrawal until Hezbollah is disarmed throughout the country - a condition the Lebanese state has never been able to meet, which makes the presence open-ended by construction. The desk that decides is not the cabinet podium but Northern Command's force-generation math and the finance ministry's reserve-duty bill, because holding ground costs manpower in a way air power does not. Note also the direction this cuts: history says a held buffer produces chronic attrition rather than episodic campaigns, which is why this board CUT its multi-week-campaign odds on the day the zone was declared. Separately, national security minister Ben Gvir published a twenty-page plan for what he calls voluntary emigration of Gaza's population - 250,000 in the first year and the remainder over six more. It is a minister's document rather than cabinet policy, and forced transfer of civilians from occupied territory is a war crime under the Geneva Conventions; it is logged here as a coalition signal, not as a programme.

concerns: The 27 October election makes restraint politically expensive at exactly the wrong moment
A withdrawal condition the Lebanese state cannot satisfy converts an operation into an occupation by definition
The Lebanon framework still has no third-party verifier and the party being disarmed rejects the premise
Ministerial transfer plans for Gaza, even unimplemented, carry legal and coalition exposure that outlasts the cabinet

dossiers.name: Germany

glance.government: Federal parliamentary republic; sixteen Laender, each electing its own Minister-President. Berlin and Mecklenburg-Vorpommern vote 20 September 2026
glance.leader: Friedrich Merz, chancellor, whose CDU just lost 25 of its 40 seats in Saxony-Anhalt; Ulrich Siegmund leads the AfD there and has said he will not stand for Minister-President without a stable majority
glance.gdp: Roughly $4.9tn nominal - unverified against a current print; Jaguar Land Rover cutting 4,000 jobs and Volkswagen repurposing a plant for defence are the texture of the industrial quarter
glance.military: About 182,000 active on standard counts, with rearmament running against recruitment shortfalls; unverified against a current IISS figure
glance.influence: Europe's largest industrial gas consumer, the logistics bridge to Ukraine through Leipzig/Halle, and the swing vote on every EU sanctions and energy instrument

dossiers.summary: Germany's constraint stopped being abstract on Sunday. The AfD took 43.9 per cent and 39 of 83 seats in Saxony-Anhalt on turnout that rose from about 60 to about 80 per cent, and the CDU fell to 17.2 per cent - which means the late-mobilisation argument that has contained the AfD in every previous Land election did not work, and ING said so in as many words. The desk that now decides is not the federal party presidium in Berlin, which can only expel people; it is the Landtag running ballots in Magdeburg, where a third round for Minister-President is settled by a simple majority of votes cast and the five-seat BSW can decide the outcome by abstaining. Underneath the politics the older vice is unchanged: Germany replaced Russian pipeline gas with seaborne LNG, trading a political dependency for a maritime one, so a war at Hormuz reaches German industry directly - and it remains the physical bridge over which munitions reach Ukraine, which is why a drone came down at Leipzig/Halle rather than at a barracks. Two more elections land on 20 September.

concerns: A Land where no majority exists without breaking one of two taboos - the CDU has excluded both the AfD and Die Linke, and the third-ballot rule rewards deadlock
Berlin and Mecklenburg-Vorpommern vote on 20 September, thirteen days after the mobilisation defence visibly failed
Fraud narratives spread within hours of the count, part of them traced by DW's fact-check desk to the Matryoshka influence operation - contested results are now a standing feature of German elections
A sabotage campaign aimed at logistics rather than forces sits deliberately below any alliance threshold, and Lavrov has answered Berlin's attribution by calling it the start of a real war
Energy input cost remains the binding industrial number, and seaborne LNG means Hormuz is now a German domestic-politics variable

dossiers.name: United States

glance.government: Federal presidential republic; midterm elections 3 November 2026
glance.leader: Donald Trump; Scott Bessent at Treasury, Marco Rubio at State, Pete Hegseth at Defense, Kevin Warsh at the Federal Reserve
glance.gdp: Roughly $30tn nominal on standard 2026 estimates - unverified against a current print; federal debt past $40tn
glance.military: About 1.34 million active with roughly 770,000 reserve and National Guard; budget in the $900bn range
glance.influence: Dollar clearing and OFAC designations, CENTCOM escort of the strait, and a rate path that prices everyone else's oil bill

dossiers.summary: The American constraint hardened today and it is arithmetic rather than politics. August payrolls came in at 162,000 against a 53,000 consensus with unemployment at 4.1%, which removes the soft-landing argument for cutting; simultaneously diesel set an all-time record at $5.820 a gallon on a refining shortage no interest rate can fix. That is the RESCUE WITHHELD configuration - a market pricing help in a shock where help does not exist - and the long end already agrees, with the ten-year at 4.79% and the thirty-year at 5.27%, both above this board's published red lines, and the reverse-repo buffer down to $0.70bn. The desk that decides is not the podium: it is the FOMC, the refiners' turnaround calendar and the weekly EIA distillate print, in that order of who can actually change the number. Foreign policy is being run on the same logic - allies invoiced for contributions at Hormuz, a Venezuelan venture organised around one man's legal exposure rather than around built infrastructure, and a president who declined this week to say whether the United States would defend Britain in another Falklands war. Each of those is leverage bought cheaply now against a commitment payable later.

concerns: Record diesel is the invisible half of the inflation problem, because it prices freight, farming and heating rather than only the pump
A hot labour print into a hiking debate removes the monetary rescue markets keep assuming
Enforcement at Hormuz is now a standing commitment - a lane you must keep clearing is not a victory
Alliance ambiguity is being used as leverage in three theatres at once, and credibility spent in one is not recoverable in another
Confirmed American casualties would collapse the intercepted-volley equilibrium the whole restraint posture rests on

dossiers.name: Japan

glance.government: Constitutional monarchy with a parliamentary system; Bank of Japan policy decision due 18 September 2026
glance.leader: Emperor Naruhito as head of state; the offices that matter for this file are the Bank of Japan policy board and the Ministry of Finance FX desk - not the cabinet
glance.gdp: Roughly $4.2tn nominal on standard 2026 estimates - unverified against a current print; policy rate 0.75 per cent, a thirty-year high, with ten-year government bond yields near 3 per cent for the first time since 1996
glance.military: Self-Defense Forces of about 247,000 active personnel; defence spending on a path toward 2 per cent of GDP
glance.influence: The world's cheap funding currency, one of the largest foreign holders of US Treasuries, and a carry trade estimated anywhere between $500bn and over $4tn depending on definition

dossiers.summary: Japan's constraint became visible in a number this week: 15.4 trillion yen, about $98.6bn, spent in a single month defending the currency, and reporting that it likely sold US Treasuries to fund it. For thirty years Japan supplied the world with money that cost nothing and the world spent it on everything from Mexican bonds to American technology; that arrangement is unwinding because Japan finally has inflation, imported partly through a weak yen and partly through an energy bill that this year's Hormuz disruption made worse. The desk that decides is the BoJ policy board on 18 September, and the yen has already run to 154.06 on the expectation. What is genuinely new is the American side of the plumbing: Washington joined the July intervention and Bessent pushed the Fed to widen the FIMA repo facility, which lets Tokyo borrow dollars against its Treasuries instead of selling them. Read that as the balance-of-financial-terror being actively managed - the US needs its largest foreign creditor not to become a seller during a heavy issuance calendar, and it built a valve to make sure.

concerns: A disorderly carry unwind transmits a Tokyo rate decision into global asset prices within hours, as it did in August 2024
The size of the borrowed-yen stack is genuinely unknown - published estimates span an order of magnitude
A currency defence funded by Treasury sales raises US long-end yields at the exact moment the ten-year sits above 4.75 per cent
A defence financed by repo must be repeatedly refinanced, which converts a one-off intervention into a standing obligation
Imported energy costs are the transmission line from the Strait of Hormuz into Japanese inflation and therefore into this policy decision

scenarios.q: What if the BSW abstains in Magdeburg?
scenarios.read: This branch stopped being hypothetical last night and it runs on a ballot rule rather than on sentiment. Saxony-Anhalt elects its Minister-President by absolute majority in the first two rounds - which nobody can reach in a chamber split 39 AfD, 39 firewall parties, 5 BSW - and by a SIMPLE MAJORITY OF VOTES CAST in the third. Abstention is therefore not neutrality; it is a decision, and five people can make it. The firewall's 39 is also not a bloc: the CDU has excluded both the AfD and Die Linke, so the alternative majority requires the CDU to break a second taboo in order to preserve the first. Stage A of the previous version of this branch, written before the vote, resolved YES: the AfD took the most seats and fell short of an absolute majority, at 39 of the 42 needed.

stages.s: Within 60 days: government-formation talks fail to produce an absolute majority for any candidate and the Landtag proceeds toward a third ballot. Falsifier: a CDU-led coalition or a stable minority arrangement agreed and announced before the constitutive deadline.

Within 120 days: a published BSW abstention or toleration understanding, or a CDU arrangement with Die Linke that breaks the second taboo. Falsifier: the BSW committing in writing to vote against any AfD candidate in every round.
Within 18 months: an AfD Minister-President sworn in anywhere in Germany - GEO-028, raised to 23 per cent today. Falsifier: a government seated in Magdeburg that survives a budget vote.
Beyond: the federal CDU formally softens the Brandmauer at Land level rather than expelling those who breach it. Most branches die at stage A or B and this one is written to.

scenarios.falsifier: A conventional coalition or stable CDU minority government seated in Magdeburg within 90 days kills this branch, returns GEO-028 to 16 and scores today's seven-point raise a miss. Thuringia 2020 is the precedent for fast federal reversal and it is the reason this is at 23 and not at 40.

scenarios.q: What if Iran's restricted zone becomes an administration rather than a threat?
scenarios.read: The penalty Iran chose is the tell. It is not promising to sink vessels that enter the new zone - it is promising to LIST them, which is an instrument that works on underwriters and charterers rather than on captains, and which survives a ceasefire because a registry costs nothing to maintain. Ostovar's thesis is that the IRGC converts every crisis into an institution, and the Persian Gulf Strait Authority already did this for the strait; the zone extends the same machinery to Gulf waters starting at the US Navy's own blockade line, which makes every American escort transit a claimed violation by construction. The physical evidence is that the coercion works even where enforcement is thin: 9M b/d against 20 pre-conflict, 5-11 ships a day against roughly 130.

stages.s: Within 14 days: Iran publishes actual coordinates, or Oman co-signs a corridor map. Falsifier: no map by 22 September, which scores this as a bargaining position rather than an administration and marks the escalation read down.

Within 60 days: a first vessel is publicly named on the Iranian list, or a war-risk syndicate reprices the zone separately from the strait. The insurer's move is the one that matters - it is the desk that actually decides whether a hull sails.
Within 6 months: any US-Iran arrangement leaves the transit-administration machinery standing - GEO-013 at 76 per cent. Note this stage does not require a deal, only that any deal has this shape.

Beyond: a strike on Kharg's LOADING TERMINALS rather than its ships, which ends Iranian seaborne export rather than taxing it, and takes the zone question off the table by removing the thing being taxed. Wired separately because most branches die earlier.

scenarios.falsifier: Fourteen days with no coordinates, no Omani co-signature and no listed vessel kills the administration read and returns this to a rhetorical zone - scored, not deferred.

scenarios.q: What if Japan's currency defence becomes a Treasury-funding problem?
scenarios.read: Tokyo spent a record 15.4 trillion yen, about $98.6bn, in the month to 26 August, and reporting now says it likely sold US Treasuries to do it. The mechanism is direct: a large foreign official holder liquidating reserve assets raises the yield on the instrument the US must roll, with the ten-year already at 4.77 per cent. Washington's answer was to join the intervention and to push the Fed to widen the FIMA repo facility, which lets a foreign central bank borrow dollars AGAINST its Treasuries rather than sell them. This is the balance-of-financial-terror being actively managed rather than merely described - and the second-order effect is the carry trade, thirty years of the world borrowing yen at nothing, which reprices when the cheap leg stops being cheap.

stages.s: Within 12 days: the BoJ raises on 18 September and the yen holds under 155. Falsifier: a hold that sends it back through 158, which scores today's GEO-025 raise a miss.

Within 30 days: the yen reaches 147.2 or below, an 8 per cent move from 160 - GEO-025, raised to 29 today. The August 2024 template needed a Tokyo surprise AND a dovish Fed, and with GEO-029 at 63 per cent to hike, only one leg is live.

Within 90 days: a second month of Japanese foreign-securities sales in the reserve data, or a visible jump in FIMA usage. These are ALTERNATIVES with opposite effects on the US long end, and which one appears is the finding. Falsifier: neither, which says the July operation ended the pressure.

Beyond: a disorderly unwind transmitting a Tokyo decision into global asset prices within hours, as in August 2024. Most branches die at stage A or B; this is written so the tail is priced, not predicted.

scenarios.q: What if the Fed hikes into an oil supply shock?
scenarios.read: The branch nobody is watching, and it sits under every other story on this board. The mechanism is a category error with a long pedigree: an oil-driven price rise is a SUPPLY event and a policy rate is a DEMAND instrument, so tightening against it treats the symptom in the only place the tool reaches. Blinder and Bernanke's work on supply shocks is the standing argument for looking through it; three FOMC members dissented for a hike anyway in July, PCE runs 3.7 per cent, and Brent is at $97.47 because OPEC+ declined to add October barrels and most of its spare capacity sits behind the contested strait. The second-order effect now runs the other way from last week: a hawkish Fed widens the dollar-yen differential and suppresses the carry unwind, which is the single largest thing holding GEO-025 down.

stages.s: Within 9 days: a 25bp increase on 16 September. Falsifier: a hold with the dissent bloc shrinking, which sends GEO-029 to 45 and is scored, not deferred.

Within 90 days: the ten-year holds above 4.75 and the thirty-year above 5.25 for a full month with the bill programme still running. Falsifier: the long end falling back through both lines, which would say the market read the hike as credibility rather than as fiscal strain.

Within 6 months: a funding event rather than a price move - a heavily tailed thirty-year auction or visible dealer balance-sheet strain. Falsifier: six months of clean auctions scores the strain read a miss.
Beyond: the standing bill programme is expanded or renamed rather than sunset - GEO-019 at 93 per cent. Most branches die at stage A or B and this one is written to.

chatter.claim: That 23 September 2026 is the start date of a mass-extinction event and that the die-off has already begun quietly - insect collapse, ocean anoxia and a coming solar 'micronova' are cited together as evidence that a threshold was crossed and is being managed rather than announced.
chatter.spread: The loudest non-general thread on /pol/ this evening at over 300 replies, running alongside a separate micronova thread at 118; the same date is circulating on collapse-oriented X accounts.
chatter.read: This is the dated-apocalypse frame, which has a reliable structure: a precise near-date, ordinary observables reinterpreted as signs, and a claim that authorities know. The checkable kernel is real and mundane - insect biomass decline and ocean deoxygenation are both measured, published phenomena - and the move is to attach a measured slow trend to an unmeasured fast date. Note the date sits on the equinox, which is where this genre usually anchors.

chatter.claim: That the drone incident at Leipzig/Halle airport in August was staged by Germany itself and blamed on Russia - the argument being that none of the drones detonated, that one was found by a lorry driver stepping on it, and that a real sabotage drone would have exploded, so the incident was manufactured to license diplomatic escalation.
chatter.spread: A /pol/ thread titled 'most european false flag imaginable', resurfaced today because Moscow cited that same incident when ordering German missions closed; amplified on German-language Telegram.
chatter.read: The false-flag frame applied to an attribution gap, and it is downstream of a genuine problem: drone-incursion attribution in Europe is slow, classified and frequently never published, which leaves a vacuum this narrative fills within hours. The checkable kernel is the non-detonation detail, which is real and has not been publicly explained; the leap is from unexplained to staged.

chatter.claim: That artificial general intelligence has already been reached and is being withheld - a claim attributed to Nvidia's chief executive that OpenAI has crossed the AGI threshold is being read as proof that capability announcements now lag capability by months and that the public is being managed through a staged reveal.
chatter.spread: Two large /pol/ threads ('NVIDIA CEO confirms OpenAI has reached AGI status' at 254 replies, 'AGI IS HERE HAPPENING' at 133) citing a screenshotted X post, spilling into /biz/ where it is being traded as a signal.
chatter.read: The staged-disclosure frame, structurally identical to the one used for UFO material, and downstream of a real information asymmetry: frontier labs do evaluate models internally for months before release. The kernel worth checking is the attribution itself - a single screenshot is doing all the load-bearing work and no lab has published such a claim.

chatter.claim: That the United States has claimed the Moon and that this voids the Outer Space Treaty - the argument being that the claim passes without objection only because Washington still sets the rules, and that a Chinese equivalent would be treated as an act of war.
chatter.spread: A /pol/ thread at over 240 replies, carried from the weekend and still high in the catalog.
chatter.read: The double-standard frame, and unusually for this section the underlying legal question is genuine: Article II of the Outer Space Treaty bars national appropriation and the treaty has no enforcement organ, so a claim's legal status is decided by whether anyone protests. The board has the mechanism right and is wrong to read the absence of protest as a plot rather than as a toothless instrument.

chatter.claim: That Volkswagen converting an Osnabrueck plant to defence production is evidence of foreign capture of German industry - 'the Wagon of the Folk' being turned into a weapons line, with the plant described on the board as being handed to Israel while car production is withdrawn from ordinary Germans.
chatter.spread: A /pol/ thread linking the NDR report on Osnabrueck, running alongside today's Reuters story that VW has found a defence future for a German site; several hundred combined replies across the German-language threads.
chatter.read: An economic-nationalist capture frame attached to a real and verifiable industrial event - VW is genuinely converting capacity, and German rearmament spending is genuinely the only growth market an idle plant can reach. The ownership claim is the invented part. The underlying observation, that a consumer-industrial base is being repriced as a defence-industrial one, is simply true and is the more important story.

chatter.claim: That the yen's move is a controlled demolition rather than a market event - the currency is described as having been 'rugged' on cue, with Japan's record intervention and its likely Treasury sales presented as a coordinated operation run to Washington's timetable ahead of the Federal Reserve and Bank of Japan meetings.
chatter.spread: A /biz/ thread titled 'The Yen RUGGED' alongside the standing stock-market and precious-metals generals, which are that board's busiest threads tonight; echoed by macro accounts on X.
chatter.read: The coordinated-demolition frame applied to an intervention that was in fact openly coordinated - the July operation was jointly announced, which is exactly what makes this narrative sticky. The kernel is checkable and will be checked: Japan's monthly reserve figures show whether foreign securities were sold, and the September print is the test. What the frame adds, and cannot support, is intent.

chatter.claim: That the 9/11 attacks were foreknown and that the visual record proves it - a thread built on a single observation, that pedestrians in archival images are walking close to the towers 'like nothing happened', is being used to argue the footage was staged or edited.
chatter.spread: A /pol/ thread at nearly 180 replies four days before the anniversary, with the annual revival visible across /x/'s memory-holed threads and on anniversary-timed X accounts.
chatter.read: Anomaly-hunting in its purest form - one uninterpretable detail treated as load-bearing - and it runs on a calendar rather than on evidence, which is why it reappears in the first week of September every year. Worth logging not as a claim but as a seasonal indicator: anniversary weeks reliably raise the board's appetite for foreknowledge narratives about whatever is currently happening.

chatter.claim: That Epstein was an intelligence asset and that surviving witness testimony has been deliberately poisoned - a thread juxtaposes one claimant's reptilian-shapeshifting account with others to argue that absurd testimony is seeded on purpose so credible testimony cannot be separated from it.
chatter.spread: A /pol/ thread at over 120 replies with parallel occult framing on /x/; a recurring structure on both boards.
chatter.read: The poisoned-well frame, analytically interesting because it is self-sealing: absurd content becomes evidence of a cover-up rather than evidence against the claim. The checkable kernel is the documented one - the non-prosecution agreement and the unsealed civil filings are matters of record - and the frame's function is to make the documented and the undocumentable indistinguishable.

chatter.claim: That Houthi forces have cut the road linking Taiz to the Red Sea port of Mokha and are within a few kilometres of the Al-Bireen junction toward Aden, and that this is going unreported because it complicates the Gulf shipping story.
chatter.spread: A /pol/ thread posting a movement map and claiming gains in the last 24 hours, circulating alongside the board's Israel-Iran general, which today logged reports of Yemen-Houthi exchanges of fire and another strike on Jizan.
chatter.read: The under-reported-front frame, and this is the class of board claim most likely to turn out true - Yemeni ground movements are genuinely thinly covered and are often confirmed by wires days later. Treat it as a lead, not a fact: the falsifier is specific and cheap, since a cut Taiz-Mokha road shows up in aid-convoy routing and Mokha port throughput inside about a week.

chatter.claim: That Russia is nationalising its economy by stealth - a claim running in the Ukraine threads that Moscow is seizing private companies by designating them extremist or foreign-linked, and that this is wartime confiscation dressed as law enforcement.
chatter.spread: Carried in the standing /uhg/ Ukraine general at nearly 300 replies, and boosted today by the arrest of a Moscow police general and fuel-station executives in a theft scheme, which the board reads as the same process reaching the security services.
chatter.read: The stealth-nationalisation frame, and the kernel here is stronger than the board usually manages: Russian courts have transferred a documented and growing list of private firms to state control since 2023 under a mix of privatisation-review and extremism findings. The weakness is causal - the same pattern is equally consistent with ordinary elite asset redistribution, which is the boring explanation and usually the right one.

chatter.claim: That the Indonesian eruption is the opening of an 1883 repeat and that the resulting cooling is being downplayed in advance - now merged with today's airport closures, which are read as a larger evacuation being described as a travel disruption.
chatter.spread: Carried over from overnight and re-energised by reporting that 340,000 travellers are stranded and closures extended; running on /pol/ and on collapse-oriented X accounts.
chatter.read: The suppressed-catastrophe frame, and today it acquired a real fact to attach to - the closures and the stranded numbers are confirmed. The kernel is that volcanic sulphate cooling is a real, measured mechanism with a real historical precedent; the leap is scale, since 1883 was a caldera-collapse event and nothing observed so far is in that class. Watch for this merging with the 23 September extinction thread - two narratives converging on one date is usually the sign a date is being set.

chatter.claim: An ethnic-scapegoat narrative is circulating around European deindustrialisation and the German election result, attributing energy costs, factory closures and migration policy to a named minority as a single controlling cause; a separate strand runs the same structure on Canada's economic decline.
chatter.spread: Multiple German-language and English /pol/ threads tonight, riding on the AfD result and the Volkswagen conversion story.
chatter.read: The persuasion technique is monocausal substitution: several genuinely painful and separately-caused facts - gas prices after the pipeline losses, an ageing industrial base, an immigration system with real administrative failures - are collapsed into one agent, which converts a policy argument that can be lost into an identity claim that cannot. The phenomenon is the data point and it is a live one, because it is riding a result rather than a grievance; the content is not repeated here.

easy.bottomLine: Oil is the story of the day. America hit three Iranian oil tankers over the weekend, Iran hit back at ships linked to America, and now fewer ships are willing to sail through the narrow bit of sea where a fifth of the world's oil normally passes. Traffic there is the lowest since May, and the price of oil has climbed to about $97 - close to $100, which is the number we bet on. Elsewhere: Israel widened its air strikes in Lebanon, Russia shut a German consulate to get even for Germany shutting a Russian one, North Korea launched a warship that had sunk at its own launch last year, and Belgium charged a researcher with selling chip secrets to China.
easy.risk: Still HIGH, and we did not move it. We wrote down in advance what would push us to the top level: an American killed, or an American ship confirmed hit. Neither has happened, even after a weekend of tankers being attacked in both directions. What is changing is not the danger level but the number of places it is happening at once - the Gulf, Lebanon, Russia and Germany, and Korea all moved today, and none of them moved because of the others.
easy.markets: Oil is at about $97 and the question is whether it finishes a day above $100 before 24 September. Normally when oil jumps, the big producer group opens the taps and the price falls back. This time they left production unchanged, so nothing is pushing back - and most of the spare oil they could have added sits behind the very sea lane that is blocked. That is why this rise is different from the usual scare.
brief: Oil is close to $100 because ships are afraid to sail through the Gulf, not because much oil has actually been destroyed. Iran's new trick is to say any ship entering a big area will be blacklisted - which is cheaper than shooting, and works, because insurers decide which ships sail.

Israel bombed more villages in southern Lebanon, killing at least nine on Monday after eleven the night before. Israel says it was answering drone attacks; the strikes keep landing around one hilltop it wants, and there is no neutral referee to decide who is telling the truth.

Russia ordered a German consulate and three German language-and-culture centres to close, because Germany closed a Russian consulate first. Each side is spending the cheapest thing it owns - but these are exactly the offices you would need if the two countries ever wanted to talk quietly.

North Korea put a big new warship into service - the same one that fell over and half-sank when they first tried to launch it last year. Russia appears to have helped build it, payment for the soldiers North Korea sent to fight in Ukraine. They also opened their first road bridge to each other.

Belgium charged a researcher with taking chip secrets to China from a Belgian company that had already gone bankrupt. Bankrupt companies are the easiest place to steal technology from, because nobody is left who is paid to protect it - and Europe's rules only guard companies that are still alive.

risk.line: HIGH, unchanged for a fifth session, and the published gate is again the reason rather than the mood. This board raises to CRITICAL on a struck US-flagged hull or a confirmed American death; a weekend of US strikes on three Iranian tankers, Iranian counter-strikes on US-linked vessels and an Iranian restricted-zone announcement beginning at the US Navy's own blockade line has produced neither, and CENTCOM today denied an Iranian claim about an uncrewed US vessel. What changed by this evening is BREADTH rather than depth, and that is worth stating plainly because it is the thing a single-theatre board would miss. Brent traded near $97.4 - about a dollar over Friday's $96.28 settle, roughly 8 per cent up on the week - with Hormuz commodity transits at their lowest since May and OPEC+ having left October output unchanged, which removes the mechanism that normally caps a geopolitical rally. Israel widened its Lebanon campaign to at least nine dead on Monday after eleven overnight, still clustered on one ridge above Nabatieh. Moscow ordered Germany's St Petersburg consulate and three Goethe-Instituts closed, five days after Berlin closed Russia's Bonn consulate over an August drone incident that has still not been publicly attributed. North Korea commissioned a salvaged 5,000-tonne destroyer and fired about ten short-range missiles as the US, South Korea and Japan opened Freedom Edge. Belgium charged a researcher over gallium nitride process secrets bound for Beijing. Five theatres, five separate causal chains, one evening - and the ten-day convergence is unchanged: FOMC on the 16th, BoJ on the 18th, Berlin and Mecklenburg-Vorpommern on the 20th, the Xi summit and Brent's resolution on the 24th.

forecasts.q: An AfD politician is sworn in as Minister-President of a German Land
forecasts.note: RAISED 7, the largest single move this book has made, and it is written down as a deliberate exception to the small-moves rule with its reason attached. The question was opened on 5 September specifically so a result would score it rather than be back-fitted, and the result beat the polls: AfD 43.9 per cent against a polled 41.8, 39 of 83 seats, CDU collapsing 25 seats to 15. What bought the points is not the vote share, it is the BALLOT RULE. Saxony-Anhalt elects a Minister-President by absolute majority in the first two rounds and by a SIMPLE MAJORITY OF VOTES CAST in the third. The chamber splits 39 AfD, 39 firewall parties, 5 BSW - and the CDU has excluded both the AfD and Die Linke, so the 39 opposite is four parties that have already excluded each other. Abstention alone can seat an AfD candidate. Framework: Tsebelis on veto players, plus the plain point that a cordon sanitaire is a coalition instrument and is silent about a ballot procedure. ANCHOR RECOMPUTED 5 to 12 today with its inputs published per the 6 September rule: the 5 was a 77-year zero-occurrence base rate across sixteen Laender, which remains the correct reference class and is why this is at 23 rather than 40, but it must now be conditioned on a chamber where the arithmetic permits it and a fallback rule that exists. Held down by two hard facts: Siegmund has said he will not stand without a stable majority, and the Thuringia 2020 precedent - an FDP minister-president briefly elected with AfD votes - collapsed within days under federal pressure, which is evidence that informal enforcement is real and fast. FALSIFIER: a conventional coalition or stable CDU minority government seated in Magdeburg within 90 days returns this to 16 and scores the raise a miss.

forecasts.q: Brent stays inside the $80-100 band
forecasts.note: CUT 4 on geometry, with the anchor recomputed the same day per the new expiry rule. Brent traded $97.47 with a $97.93 intraday high, the highest since 24 July, after rising about 8 per cent last week. ANCHOR 36 to 28, computed 7 September from spot 97.47, about 12 trading sessions to 24 September, and a continuity-corrected discrete-monitoring barrier because this question resolves on daily CLOSES and not on touches - survival is about 33 per cent at 35 per cent volatility, 28 at 45, and 24 at 60, and Brent's own realised move annualises near 60, so the vol used is published rather than assumed. The mark sits at 25, modestly below the central case, for one named reason that is a drift term rather than a vol term: OPEC+ removed the capping mechanism when it left October output unchanged, and most of its spare capacity sits behind the contested strait, so the usual mean-reverting supply response is not available. Stated against my own move: this is a barrier question three weeks from resolution and small changes in the vol assumption swing it by nine points, which is why confidence stays Low-Mod. The $97.93 was an INTRADAY print and does not touch this question - restated for the seventh time because it is the difference between a Brier score and a non-score.

forecasts.q: Yen carry stress: USD/JPY appreciates 8%+ (160 to 147.2 or below) in any 30-day window
forecasts.note: RAISED 5, reversing yesterday's audit cut, and the reason is a price print rather than a narrative. The yen went to 154.06, its strongest since late February and PAST the peak of the July joint intervention, which means about 3.7 of the required 8 per cent is already done and the remaining 4.5 has roughly 26 days of this rolling window plus every window after it. ANCHOR RECOMPUTED 18 to 28 today with inputs, because the observable has moved more than one standard deviation since the anchor was set: spot 154.06, barrier 147.2, BoJ decision 18 September INSIDE the window, and a base rate in which 8 per cent 30-day yen appreciations are rare but recurrent - August 2024, the October-December 2022 intervention run, 1998. Two mechanisms now push and one pulls. PUSH: BoJ hike expectations into 18 September, and a Ministry of Finance that has already spent a record 15.4 trillion yen and likely sold US Treasuries to do it, which is a state demonstrating it will act. PULL, and it is why this is 29 and not 40: the August 2024 template needed BOTH a Tokyo surprise AND a dovish repricing of the Fed, and GEO-029 has the Fed at 63 per cent to HIKE on 16 September, which removes the second leg. FALSIFIER: a BoJ hold on 18 September that sends the yen back through 158 scores this raise a miss.

forecasts.q: Israel-Hezbollah escalates to multi-week campaign
forecasts.note: RAISED 3 on TEMPO, and the note is mostly about what did NOT buy the points. Eleven killed overnight including two infants, after seven the previous day: eighteen in two days is the deadliest stretch since the June truce, beating the 11 of 15 August. That is the raise. The Ali al-Taher ridge is explicitly NOT counted - Israel announced clearing its tunnels on Friday 4 September, three days ago, and its own June security-zone map already included the ridge, so treating it as new evidence today would be pricing something that belonged in June. Framework: Fortna on ceasefire durability - this truce has no demarcation line, no monitor and no guarantor in operating form, and ceasefires without monitoring break at roughly twice the rate of those with it, with grinding attrition as the modal failure rather than declared collapse. The disputed attribution is itself the structural finding: Israel says it intercepted rockets, Hezbollah says it did not fire them, and no third party is empowered to adjudicate. Held to +3 because the question resolves on a MULTI-WEEK campaign north of the Litani, which is a different object from a lethal fortnight. FALSIFIER: fourteen days with no comparable multi-death strike day returns this to 30, scored as a miss.

forecasts.q: Major US/Israeli strike campaign on Iran resumes
forecasts.note: RAISED 2 on SCOPE rather than on the tanker strikes, which were priced yesterday and would be double-counted today. The new fact is that Iran's Supreme National Security Council announced a restricted maritime zone beginning at the US Navy blockade line and extending through Gulf waters - the permit regime moving OUTWARD from the strait - while claiming attacks on tankers and other vessels linked to the US. A declared zone that starts at the adversary's own blockade line is a collision surface by construction: it converts every US escort transit into a claimed violation. Framework: recurrence hazard, where the reference class is resumption of an already-resumed exchange rather than initiation, plus Schelling on leaving something to chance - neither party has to decide on a campaign for one to arrive. Capped at +2 and the resolution defect pinned on 6 September still stands and still binds: this resolves on MULTI-DAY strikes on STATE targets, NITC tankers are state-owned, and an interested reading could score it YES already. It is not being scored yes; the pin is restated so the ambiguity is on the record before resolution day rather than after.

forecasts.q: Hormuz transits recover past 50% of pre-war volume
forecasts.note: HELD, and this is a deliberate non-move on tempting evidence. Iran announcing a restricted zone beyond the strait is transit-negative in every intuitive sense, but this question resolves on VOLUME and an announcement is not a volume print - the same discipline that made this board refuse three tempo facts on 5 September before accepting the Kpler print on 6 September. Today's actual flow numbers are unchanged in substance: about 9M b/d against 20 pre-conflict, 5 to 11 vessels a day against roughly 130. Spending the announcement here would be double-counting it against GEO-003, where it was priced.

forecasts.q: Russia-Ukraine ceasefire holds 30+ days
forecasts.note: HELD at 20 for a second consecutive session, and the evidence today leans slightly NEGATIVE rather than positive. The Kremlin says it does not rule out a restart of talks with Ukraine and the US - which is a statement about the possibility of meeting, not about terms - and Ushakov's line that there was no talk of new ideas remains the most informative sentence out of the Moscow session. Witkoff called Kyiv substantive and encouraging; adjectives are not a text. Fortna's guarantor requirement is used here again as a reason NOT to move: no demarcation line, no named monitor, no guarantor instrument has been published. The dated falsifier runs out tomorrow when the 72-hour capitals pause expires, and if it lapses with nothing published the 3 September raise is scored a miss and this goes to 17.

forecasts.q: US diesel crack spread settles back below $45/bbl before 15 Dec 2026
forecasts.note: HELD, explicitly, on a day that supplied the most vivid illustration yet of its own mechanism. The bunker-fuel squeeze - Singapore VLSFO up 76 per cent to about $825 a tonne, Rotterdam and Fujairah stocks 30 per cent below seasonal norms - is caused by refiners reconfiguring toward diesel because the crack is at records. That is the SAME conversion constraint that bought Friday's cut from 35 to 32, arriving in a different product. Re-marking on a downstream consequence of an argument already priced is the double-count this board named on 6 September, so the number stays. Sits 13 points below its anchor with the reason on the record: refining capital stock responds in years, crude valves in weeks.

forecasts.q: IF a Hormuz deal happens, it preserves Iranian transit administration
forecasts.note: HELD, and the restraint is worth naming. Iran choosing SANCTIONS-LISTING as the penalty for entering its new zone, and coordinating corridor maps with Oman, is exactly the administrative-instrument behaviour Ostovar's thesis predicts - a registry rather than a navy.
